examples/testkit/ts.mjs.description: TypeScript testkit example: HTTP API v2 request/response, EventBridge workload envelopes and schedules, and DynamoDB stream normalization, all in process with no AWS.

examples/testkit/ts-streaming.mjs.description: TypeScript testkit streaming example: Lambda Function URL streaming chunks, cookies, header mutation and late-error framing.

examples/testkit/py.py.description: Python testkit example: HTTP API v2 request/response, EventBridge workload envelopes and schedules, and DynamoDB stream normalization, all in process with no AWS.

examples/mcp/tools-only-ts/server.mjs.description: TypeScript MCP Streamable HTTP server: initialize, tools/list, tools/call and the exported Lambda entry, driven by the real server and the MCP testkit.

examples/mcp/tools-only-py/server.py.description: Python MCP Streamable HTTP server: initialize, tools/list, tools/call and the exported Lambda entry, driven by the real server and the MCP testkit.

examples/mcp/tools-only/main.go.description: Go MCP tools-only server: the real binary runs in a warm provided.al2023 container and is driven with explicit MCP HTTP API v2 events (initialize, tools/list, tools/call and two JSON-RPC refusals). Handler-only example: it ships no CDK definition, so no route table is synthesized.

examples/mcp/tools-resources-prompts/mai.description: Go MCP server exposing tools, resources and prompts: the real binary runs in a warm provided.al2023 container and is driven with explicit MCP HTTP API v2 events (tools, resources/read, prompts/get and a refusal). Handler-only example: it ships no CDK definition.

examples/mcp/resumable-sse/main.go.gap: Incremental SSE delivery; the RIE buffers the complete stream. Session creation, event IDs and Last-Event-ID replay are asserted on a warm container.
examples/mcp/resumable-sse/main.go.description: Go MCP resumable SSE server: a warm provided.al2023 container keeps the session, the buffered tool-call stream carries priming/progress/result IDs, and Last-Event-ID replay returns the progress events and final result. Handler-only example: it ships no CDK definition, so no route table is synthesized.

examples/migration/rate-limited-http/mai.description: Lift-to-AppTheory migration server as a real net/http process on DynamoDB Local: real pkg/limited middleware, the rate-limits table provisioned from the real model, 60 allowed requests and the 429 refusal.

examples/cdk/hello-world/bin/apptheory-h.description: CDK app anchor for the synth row: every CDK example in the tree is synthesized and compared with its pinned template hash (plus focused construct assertions for the six once-uncovered examples, and an official Lambda runtime image invocation of the staged TypeScript and Python assets).

examples/cdk/hello-world/handlers/go/mai.description: hello-world Go handler: the app's synthesized CDK stack, the provided.al2023 arm64 container through the Runtime Interface Emulator, and four HTTP assertions over the derived HTTP API v2 transport (request id, root, 405, 404).

examples/cdk/hello-world/handlers/py/han.description: hello-world Python handler: the app's synthesized CDK stack, the python:3.14 container through the Runtime Interface Emulator, and four HTTP assertions over the derived HTTP API v2 transport.

examples/cdk/hello-world/handlers/ts/han.description: hello-world TypeScript handler: the app's synthesized CDK stack, the nodejs:24 container through the Runtime Interface Emulator, and four HTTP assertions over the derived HTTP API v2 transport.

examples/cdk/hello-world/handlers/ts/app.description: hello-world TypeScript app module imported by the handler; exercised through the same HTTP assertions.

examples/cdk/import-pipeline/bin/app.ts.description: Import pipeline CDK app, synthesized and hash-checked with focused construct assertions.

examples/cdk/import-pipeline/handlers/in.gap: S3 → EventBridge delivery and CodeBuild; ingest runs on the DynamoDB Local jobs table and sends to ElasticMQ from a real s3proxy object.
examples/cdk/import-pipeline/handlers/in.description: Import pipeline ingest handler: the CDK IngestRule EventBridge event is built from a real object written to s3proxy; the handler writes the job meta and three work messages that are read back from ElasticMQ.

examples/cdk/import-pipeline/handlers/wo.gap: S3 → EventBridge delivery and CodeBuild; ingest and worker run end to end on the DynamoDB Local jobs table and ElasticMQ.
examples/cdk/import-pipeline/handlers/wo.description: Import pipeline worker handler: the full ingest → worker flow runs on the CDK jobs table; the three real work messages produce SUCCEEDED/FAILED records and a sanitized error envelope.

examples/cdk/kinesis-cloudwatch-logs/bin.description: Kinesis/CloudWatch Logs CDK app, synthesized and hash-checked with focused construct assertions.

examples/cdk/kinesis-cloudwatch-logs/han.gap: Managed Kinesis event-source delivery and the CloudWatch Logs subscription path; the gzip+base64 subscription payload is generated from local content.
examples/cdk/kinesis-cloudwatch-logs/han.description: Kinesis/CloudWatch Logs handler: a real gzip+base64 subscription payload is invoked and accepted, and a malformed Kinesis record is returned as its sequence-number partial failure.

examples/cdk/lambda-role/bin/app.ts.description: Lambda role CDK app, synthesized and hash-checked with focused IAM/KMS assertions, including the compiled handler asset.

examples/cdk/lambda-role/handlers/custom.gap: SSM parameter store has no local emulator; the S3 path is emulated by s3proxy (no IAM/bucket policies or event notifications).
examples/cdk/lambda-role/handlers/custom.description: lambda-role custom handler: the compiled asset runs in nodejs:24, writes and reads back an object on s3proxy, and the failed SSM lookup falls back to not-configured.

examples/cdk/lambda-role/handlers/encryp.gap: KMS is emulated by moto (no HSM, key policies or grants); the encrypt/decrypt round-trip is real.
examples/cdk/lambda-role/handlers/encryp.description: lambda-role encrypted handler: the compiled asset runs in nodejs:24 and round-trips plaintext through the emulated KMS with match=true.

examples/cdk/lambda-role/handlers/index..description: lambda-role baseline handler: the compiled asset serves the basic, tracing and dynamic functions and returns the expected 200 payload from each.

examples/cdk/lesser-parity/bin/app.ts.description: Lesser-parity CDK app, synthesized and hash-checked with focused construct assertions.

examples/cdk/lesser-parity/handlers/api..description: Lesser-parity catch-all REST handler: GET and POST assertions with resolved TABLE_NAME/QUEUE_URL values.

examples/cdk/lesser-parity/handlers/grap.description: Lesser-parity GraphQL handler: a dedicated POST route, the resolved table name, and GET falling through to the catch-all.

examples/cdk/lesser-parity/handlers/sse..gap: Incremental SSE delivery; the RIE buffers the response. Status, content type and all three events are asserted.
examples/cdk/lesser-parity/handlers/sse..description: Lesser-parity SSE handler: all three buffered events plus the declared CORS preflight from the same REST API.

examples/cdk/lesser-parity/handlers/work.gap: SQS event delivery; the worker is invoked with a generated SQS batch because this milestone has no SQS emulator.
examples/cdk/lesser-parity/handlers/work.description: Lesser-parity queue worker: a generated two-record batch is processed and the invalid record is returned as a partial batch failure.

examples/cdk/media-cdn/bin/app.ts.gap: Signed-URL verification: the private distribution is refused with A5a's named reason; the example ships no media, so a probe object is written to the provisioned public bucket. CloudFront caching and edge network.
examples/cdk/media-cdn/bin/app.ts.description: Media CDN: the public distribution serves a probe object from the local S3 emulator with its metadata; the private trusted-key-group distribution stays refused with the named signed-URL reason; missing objects return 403 under OAC.

examples/cdk/microvm-controller/bin/app..description: MicroVM controller CDK app, synthesized and hash-checked with focused construct assertions.

examples/cdk/microvm-controller/controll.gap: Managed MicroVM provider; the real CDK authorizer and controller routes run locally and every provider-backed operation stops at that boundary.
examples/cdk/microvm-controller/controll.description: MicroVM controller: the CDK authorizer refuses missing/wrong/tenant-less credentials; list/run reach the managed provider boundary; get/suspend/resume/terminate/auth-token/shell-auth-token/invoke read the TableTheory registry on DynamoDB Local and refuse a missing session.

examples/cdk/microvm-controller/workload.description: MicroVM Go workload: the built server runs as a host process and answers GET and POST with its HTTP contract.
MicroVM Python workload: the stdlib server runs as a host process and answers GET and POST with its HTTP contract.
MicroVM TypeScript workload (the built server.js shipped in the image): it runs as a host process and answers GET and POST with its HTTP contract.
MicroVM TypeScript workload source; verified through the built server.js that the image ships and the harness runs.

examples/microvm-conformance/run_local.p.gap: Managed MicroVM provider; dry-run and leak-scan pass, and the live conformance run stops at the provider boundary. No EqualToAI/Host live proof is claimed.
examples/microvm-conformance/run_local.p.description: MicroVM conformance harness: the real dry-run and token-leak scanner pass; live mode runs against the local microvm-controller, passes its auth refusals, and stops at the managed provider boundary.

examples/cdk/multilang/bin/apptheory-mul.description: Multilang CDK app, synthesized and hash-checked with focused construct assertions; the TS Lambda asset is staged self-contained (A1 asset fix).

examples/cdk/multilang/handlers/go/main..gap: WebSocket frames and managed event-source delivery; HTTP API v2, the Go-only REST v1 surface (including /sse), and the CDK SQS, DynamoDB stream and EventBridge events are verified.
examples/cdk/multilang/handlers/go/main..description: Multilang Go handler: its own HTTP API v2 listener serves root, hello, 405 and 404; the Go REST API serves hello and all three buffered SSE events; three WebSocket APIs are reported not served; SQS, a DynamoDB stream record built from a real local write, and both EventBridge rules are invoked.

examples/cdk/multilang/handlers/py/handl.gap: WebSocket frames and managed event-source delivery are not served; HTTP API v2 is verified for Python, while the REST v1 surface is defined only for the Go handler in this stack.
examples/cdk/multilang/handlers/py/handl.description: Multilang Python handler: its own HTTP API v2 listener serves root, hello, 405 and 404; the Go-only REST surface is also asserted.

examples/cdk/multilang/handlers/ts/handl.gap: WebSocket frames and managed event-source delivery are not served; HTTP API v2 is verified for TypeScript, while the REST v1 surface is defined only for the Go handler in this stack.
examples/cdk/multilang/handlers/ts/handl.description: Multilang TypeScript handler: its own HTTP API v2 listener serves root, hello, 405 and 404; the Go-only REST surface is also asserted.

examples/cdk/path-routed-frontend/bin/ap.gap: The API origin is an external custom origin and is refused locally by name; the example ships no SPA build output, so probe objects are written through the runner to the provisioned buckets. CloudFront caching and edge network.
examples/cdk/path-routed-frontend/bin/ap.description: Path-routed frontend: the generated SPA function rewrites /l and /auth to index.html, files are served unchanged, the external API origin is refused by name, POST is refused by AllowedMethods and a missing object is 403 under OAC.

examples/cdk/restv1-router/bin/app.ts.description: REST v1 router CDK app, synthesized and hash-checked with focused route, integration and stage assertions.

examples/cdk/restv1-router/handlers/api..description: REST v1 router catch-all handler: GET and POST assertions with the matched proxy path parameter.

examples/cdk/restv1-router/handlers/grap.description: REST v1 router GraphQL handler: POST query handling and GET falling through to the catch-all route.

examples/cdk/restv1-router/handlers/inve.description: REST v1 router inventory handler: GET/PUT/DELETE with path parameters, 404 refusals and the declared CORS preflight.

examples/cdk/restv1-router/handlers/sse..gap: Incremental SSE delivery; the RIE buffers the complete response. Status, content type, all 10 events and [DONE] are asserted.
examples/cdk/restv1-router/handlers/sse..description: REST v1 router SSE handler: the real streamifyResponse handler returns all 10 events and [DONE] as one buffered body.

examples/cdk/s3-vectors-semantic-search/.description: S3 Vectors semantic search CDK app, synthesized and hash-checked with focused construct assertions.

examples/cdk/s3-vectors-semantic-search/.gap: Managed S3 Vectors and Bedrock; the HTTP and auth surface runs locally, refusals are asserted, and authorized provider calls stop at the closed Bedrock endpoint.
examples/cdk/s3-vectors-semantic-search/.description: S3 Vectors semantic search handler: health reports the CDK vector index; missing/wrong auth, missing query and invalid top_k are refused; authorized seed/search reach the Bedrock boundary with vectorstore.embedding_failed.

examples/cdk/sqs-queue/bin/app.ts.description: SQS queue CDK app, synthesized and hash-checked with focused queue, DLQ, redrive and event-source-mapping assertions.

examples/cdk/sqs-queue/handlers/dlq-hand.gap: Managed SQS event-source mapping; the message is redriven by ElasticMQ after maxReceiveCount and the handler is invoked with the message actually read from the DLQ.
examples/cdk/sqs-queue/handlers/dlq-hand.description: SQS DLQ handler: events-queue redrives a failing message to events-queue-dlq after five receives; dlq-handler.mjs processes the real dead-letter message and acknowledges it.

examples/cdk/sqs-queue/handlers/producer.gap: Managed SQS event-source mapping; the producer sends to ElasticMQ through its real handler and the message is read back.
examples/cdk/sqs-queue/handlers/producer.description: SQS producer handler: the real producer sends through the AWS SQS SDK to ElasticMQ; the received message body and messageId match.

examples/cdk/sqs-queue/handlers/worker.m.gap: Managed SQS event-source mapping (polling, visibility and deletion); two messages are received from ElasticMQ and invoked as the CDK mapping's batch.
examples/cdk/sqs-queue/handlers/worker.m.description: SQS worker handler: two real ElasticMQ messages are invoked as the CDK mapping's batch; worker.mjs reports only the simulated failure as a partial batch failure.

examples/cdk/ssr-only-provided-assets-si.gap: CloudFront caching and edge network; the AWS_IAM Function URL is reached through local SigV4 OAC signing, but IAM policy evaluation is not emulated.
examples/cdk/ssr-only-provided-assets-si.description: SSR_ONLY provided assets: the real handler runs behind an AWS_IAM Function URL origin with local OAC signing and echoes the viewer request id; the provided bucket serves app.js, site.css and probe.txt; a missing object is 403 under OAC and OPTIONS is refused.

examples/cdk/ssr-site/bin/apptheory-ssr-.gap: CloudFront caching and edge network; response streaming is buffered by the RIE.
examples/cdk/ssr-site/bin/apptheory-ssr-.description: SSR site: the origin group fails over from the S3 HTML primary (403 under OAC) to the real SSR handler; viewer-request/viewer-response effects, the assets and hydrate deployments, full and ranged HEAD, conditional If-None-Match GETs, OPTIONS and the missing-object 403 are asserted through the gateway.

examples/cdk/ssr-site/scripts/generate-a.gap: CloudFront caching and edge network; the manifest is matched against the gateway response, not a deployed bucket.
examples/cdk/ssr-site/scripts/generate-a.description: SSR site asset manifest generator: runs against the real assets directory, asserts hello.txt's sha256 and byte count, then matches the served asset through the gateway to the manifest.

examples/cdk/ssr-site/scripts/upload-ass.gap: CloudFront invalidation is not exercised; s3proxy has no IAM, bucket policy or event notifications. CloudFront caching and edge network.
examples/cdk/ssr-site/scripts/upload-ass.description: SSR site asset uploader: the real AWS CLI syncs the assets and copies the generated manifest to the local s3proxy endpoint with dummy credentials; the gateway serves both with the script's cache-control and the uploaded manifest.

examples/cdk/codebuild-job-runner/bin/ap.description: CodeBuild job runner CDK app, synthesized and hash-checked with focused project, state-change-rule and grant assertions.
